where: Section 1, sentence after the dynamic-power formula
problem: The text says 'Energy per switching event is E = α C VDD2'. With α defined (correctly, just above) as the fraction of cycles in which the node switches, α C VDD² is the energy per clock cycle, not per switching event. Multiplying by α again double-counts the activity. Students will carry this into energy-per-operation sums and get answers that are too small by a factor of α.
fix: Energy per clock cycle is E = α C VDD². A single 0-to-1 switching event on that capacitance draws C VDD².

where: Section 3 DVFS paragraph, worked example 1 steps 1 and 3, and exam trap 3
problem: Squares are written as plain digits: '(V2/V1)2 × (f2/f1)', '(1.2 V)2', '0.83332 = 0.6944', 'Pdyn = α C VDD2 f'. A student reads 0.83332 as a five-digit number and VDD2 as a subscript-less variable, and the notation does not match the superscript tags used in Section 1.
fix: Use the inline tags everywhere: (V<sub>2</sub>/V<sub>1</sub>)<sup>2</sup> × (f<sub>2</sub>/f<sub>1</sub>), (1.2 V)<sup>2</sup>, 0.8333<sup>2</sup> = 0.6944, P<sub>dyn</sub> = α C V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> f.

problem: The answer says 'The off time is short compared with the wake-up time', but the data given in the question (period 10 µs, wake-up 2 µs) leaves about 8 µs off, which is four times the wake-up time. The sentence contradicts the question's own numbers and reads as an error.
fix: The off window is only a few times the wake-up time, and each wake burns extra energy plus the 2 µs of lost work. The leakage saved during that short off window may not cover the wake energy, so retention or clock gating wins for short gaps. Also state in the question whether the 10 µs is the period or the off gap.

problem: Dynamic power is attributed only to charging and discharging node capacitance. Short-circuit (direct-path) power, which flows while both input and output transistors of a gate conduct during a transition, is part of dynamic power too, and the chapter never mentions it.
fix: Add one line: dynamic power has two parts, switching power α C V<sub>DD</sub><sup>2</sup> f and short-circuit power from the brief period when both nMOS and pMOS of a gate conduct. The switching part dominates and is what clock gating, power gating and DVFS attack.
